# Jincubator

> John Whitton's independent research and engineering studio for financial and distributed systems.

## Docs

- [Legacy Overview](/overview)
- [Salus](/salus): Salus is an active Jincubator research and engineering initiative and
reference implementation for decentralized trading-system architecture.
- [Archive](/archive/intro): The Archive preserves research and implementation history without presenting it as current canonical work. Individual pages may contain superseded assumptions, old interfaces, incomplete plans, or historical measurements; their original dates and context govern.
- [Backpressure and Queue Ownership](/architecture/backpressure-and-queue-ownership): High-throughput systems remain understandable when queues transport typed work while the domain owner decides freshness, coalescing, retry, ordering, and shutdown.
- [Capital-Efficient Funding Models](/architecture/capital-efficient-funding-models): Transaction-scoped funding can reduce the principal an executor must hold before a trade, but it adds availability, fee, repayment, callback, state, and failure constraints that the execution design must make explicit.
- [Evidence-Grounded AI for Trading Systems](/architecture/evidence-grounded-ai-for-trading-systems): Latency-sensitive financial systems can use predictive models and
evidence-grounded investigation without transferring execution authority to
probabilistic software.
- [Inspectable Read Models for Trading Systems](/architecture/inspectable-trading-read-models): Trading-system persistence is credible when authoritative observations, derived current views, runtime-only state, and retained evidence artifacts remain distinguishable.
- [Architecture](/architecture/intro): Current Architecture distills reusable design forces, boundaries, trade-offs, failure modes, and validation lessons from reviewed Work and Research.
- [From Liquidity State to Route Graphs](/architecture/liquidity-state-to-route-graphs): A trading system needs a stable graph and catalog boundary between changing protocol state and later strategy decisions. This architecture explains what to normalize, what to preserve, and what must remain outside the mapping layer.
- [Architecture Portfolio](/architecture/portfolio): This presentation page organizes the current generated Architecture narratives. The canonical prose and review records live in the Knowledge Base; implementation details remain with their project repositories.
- [Protocol Simulation Boundaries](/architecture/protocol-simulation-boundaries): Protocol simulation is safe to reuse when coverage, state provenance, route-local mutation, economic inputs, and failure semantics are explicit.
- [Salus Architecture: An Opinionated Rust Implementation of Web3 Trading and Solving Infrastructure](/architecture/salus-trading-and-solving-infrastructure): **Draft** — This public working document is under active independent review.
- [Designing Evidence-Aware Trading-System Pipelines](/architecture/trading-system-execution-pipelines): A trading system becomes reviewable when market state, modeled opportunities, execution decisions, and realized outcomes remain distinct. This architecture describes boundaries that preserve those distinctions without copying one implementation.
- [Engage](/engage/intro): John takes on selected, clearly bounded conversations involving:
- [Partnerships — Legacy Route](/partnerships/intro): Jincubator's current collaboration path is [Engage](/engage/intro). It covers selected research collaboration, architecture review or technical diligence, bounded prototype or implementation review, and protocol or solver collaboration where responsibilities are clear.
- [Product — Legacy Route](/product/intro): This route remains for compatibility. Current evidence-bearing work now lives under [Work](/work/intro): [Salus](/work/salus), [Digital Banking](/work/digital-banking), and [Intent Systems Prototypes](/work/prototypes).
- [Kanga Finance: Harmony Hackathon 2021](/proposals/Harmony): [kanga.finance](https://kanga.finance/) is a Dex implementation inspired by Sushi and proof of concept integration with one-wallet. ([github](https://github.com/kangafinance)). Winner of \$30,000 in prizes from [Harmony Hackathon](https://bounties.gitcoin.co/hackathon/harmony-defi/onboard).
- [IntentSwap Hook: Uniswap Hook Incubator 5 (2025)](/proposals/UHI5): Historical prototype record. Proposed integrations and roadmap items below are preserved in their 2025 context; they are not current production, partnership, or completion claims. See [Intent Systems Prototypes](/work/prototypes) for the reviewed synthesis.
- [Unite DeFi Prototype (2025)](/proposals/Unite): John and Jincubator built this as a historical 2025 hackathon prototype, not a current product. It explored how a limit-order protocol could delegate a swap through a solver payload, use approved maker or taker funds during atomic settlement, and return excess value according to the order contract's rules.
- [TAP-4 Atomic Arbitrage : Application Proposal](/proposals/atomic-arbitrage): Submitted by: [John Whitton](https://johnwhitton.com) and [Jincbator](https://jincubator.com): [john@johnwhitton.com](mailto:john@johnwhitton.com)
- [Proposals — Historical Route](/proposals/intro): This section preserves dated proposals and event submissions. Roadmaps and proposed integrations describe intent at the time; they are not evidence of completed functionality, current partnerships, production deployment, or commercial maturity.
- [Research Proposal: Solvers, Arbitrage & Intent-Based Protocols](/proposals/solving-arbitrage): Over the past eight months, I’ve developed both a solver engine and an intent-based swap protocol integrating Uniswap v4. My work spans arbitrage detection/execution, real-time streaming, solver frameworks, and resource-efficient intent mechanisms. Retained research material is accessible via [Jincubator Research](/research/intro).
- [Sunrise DEX](/proposals/sunrise): [Link to original W3 Grant Proposal](https://github.com/w3f/Grants-Program/blob/master/applications/sunrise-dex.md)
- [Prototypes — Compatibility Route](/prototypes/intro): Prototypes now live structurally under [Work](/work/prototypes). The current generated page covers the bounded UHI5 intent-hook and Unite DeFi solver experiments with explicit implementation and maturity limits.
- [Salus Architecture: An Opinionated Rust Implementation of Web3 Trading and Solving Infrastructure](/salus/architecture): **Draft** — This public working document is under active independent review.
- [Salus: Modular Trading and Solving Infrastructure for Decentralized Markets](/salus/whitepaper): **Draft** — This public working document is under active independent review.
- [Building a Polkadot Parachain — EAVE](/work/building-polkadot-parachain-eave): EAVE is a historical case study in translating an emerging-asset venture thesis into a Polkadot parachain design, then separating the architecture that was proposed from the integration that source evidence can actually support.
- [DeFi Leveraging](/work/defi-leveraging): DeFi Leveraging is a bounded case study in designing leverage-token accounting, automated position rebalancing, and intent-based execution without confusing protocol safety with off-chain strategy.
- [DeFi Protocol Engineering — Kanga](/work/defi-protocol-engineering-kanga): Kanga is a historical DeFi protocol case study that connects John's documented product and protocol design with a source-backed automated-market-maker, incentive, staking, fee-conversion, and liquidity-migration architecture.
- [Digital Banking Reference Implementation](/work/digital-banking): Digital Banking is John Whitton's non-production reference implementation for durable digital-asset settlement control planes across local Ethereum and Solana environments.
- [Enterprise SOA](/work/enterprise-soa): Enterprise SOA is a domain-based case study of the integration platforms John designed and delivered to connect core business systems, partner rails, customer workflows, and production operations without turning every dependency into a point-to-point interface.
- [Work](/work/intro): Selected Work explains what was built, who owns the implementation, what the evidence establishes, and where the current boundary stops.
- [Intent Systems Prototypes](/work/prototypes): Intent Systems Prototypes is a bounded record of experiments in turning a user's desired outcome into an authorized, constrained execution that another actor can coordinate and perform.
- [Salus](/work/salus): Salus is an active Jincubator research and engineering initiative and
reference implementation for decentralized trading-system architecture.
- [Stablecoin Intents](/work/stablecoin-intents): Stablecoin Intents is a bounded case study in coordinating source-chain rewards, destination-chain fulfillment, and proof-backed settlement across a multi-chain system.
- [Deterministic Replay as Engineering Evidence](/research/deterministic-replay-as-engineering-evidence): Replay can make an engineering result repeatable, but only within the inputs, state, code, and external dependencies actually retained. This research asks what a deterministic replay can legitimately prove.
- [High-Performance Route Evaluation](/research/high-performance-route-evaluation): Route-evaluation throughput is useful evidence only when the measured subject, workload, revision, and stopping point are explicit. This analysis interprets retained Salus measurements without treating catalog size or evaluator speed as evidence of execution or profit.
- [Research](/research/intro): Current Research answers bounded engineering questions from reviewed sources. It stays separate from implementation truth and from historical notes whose freshness or evidence boundary is no longer current.
- [What Trading-System Validation Evidence Can Prove](/research/trading-system-validation-evidence): Trading systems need layered validation because no single test, replay, comparison, preflight, receipt, or metric spans the path from code correctness to realized economic outcome.

- [Solver Roadmap — Historical Route](/product/solving/roadmap): The former roadmap described a superseded implementation sequence and is preserved in Git history rather than presented as current status.
- [Route Evaluation](/product/solving/routes): This implemented research component models tokens and pool components as a graph, generates bounded candidate paths, and evaluates affected subsets against observed state.
- [Strategy Boundary](/product/solving/strategies): This active research interface consumes normalized state and candidate routes, produces evaluations, and passes structured results to later simulation or execution boundaries. Generated candidates, filtered signals, simulations, submissions, inclusions, and realized outcomes remain distinct records.
- [Overview](/research/Intents/architecture): This is an opinionated architecture for an intent based solving protocol which facilitates single- and multichain solving of intents. Flash liquidity can remove the need to pre-fund trading principal. Infrastructure, data/RPC, operational, and transaction-gas costs still exist; reverted, unsuccessful, or non-included attempts may leave unreimbursed costs.

- [Solving and Arbitrage Research](/research/Intents/intro): Historical research route retained for compatibility. Current intent research is [Intent-Based Execution](/research/defi-protocol-engineering/intro).
- [Protocol](/research/Intents/protocol): The Protocol is part of an opinionated architecture for an intent based solving protocol which facilitates single- and multichain solving of intents. Flash liquidity can remove the need to pre-fund trading principal. Infrastructure, data/RPC, operational, and transaction-gas costs still exist; reverted, unsuccessful, or non-included attempts may leave unreimbursed costs. The design introduces a SolverPayload which can be executed by the Arbiter to ensure the EIP-712 signed mandate is met.
- [Resource Management](/research/Intents/resources): The Protocol leverages an expansive locking system from [the-compact](https://github.com/jincubator/the-compact/). Flash liquidity can remove the need to pre-fund trading principal. Infrastructure, data/RPC, operational, and transaction-gas costs still exist; reverted, unsuccessful, or non-included attempts may leave unreimbursed costs. [Mandates and Solver Payloads](/research/Intents/protocol) describe the proposed execution design.

- [Solving and Arbitrage Research](/research/deprecated/intro): Work in 2025 on Solving, Arbitrage and Indexing using [Tycho](https://docs.propellerheads.xyz/tycho/overview), Intents using [ERC-7683](https://www.erc7683.org/spec), [EIP-712](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712), [Compactx](https://github.com/uniswap/compactx) and [Uniswap V4 Hooks](https://docs.uniswap.org/contracts/v4/overview). Development can be found in the github organization [jincubator](https://github.com/jincubator).
- [Protocol](/research/deprecated/protocol): The Protocol is part of an opinionated architecture for an intent based solving protocol which facilitates single- and multichain solving of intents. Flash liquidity can remove the need to pre-fund trading principal. Infrastructure, data/RPC, operational, and transaction-gas costs still exist; reverted, unsuccessful, or non-included attempts may leave unreimbursed costs. The design introduces a SolverPayload which can be executed by the Arbiter to ensure the EIP-712 signed mandate is met.
- [Resource Management](/research/deprecated/resources): The Protocol leverages an expansive locking system from [the-compact](https://github.com/jincubator/the-compact/). Flash liquidity can remove the need to pre-fund trading principal. Infrastructure, data/RPC, operational, and transaction-gas costs still exist; reverted, unsuccessful, or non-included attempts may leave unreimbursed costs. [Mandates and Solver Payloads](/research/Intents/protocol) describe the proposed execution design.
